source_caption:
For the devastating flashback where Teddy Daniels discovers his wife has drowned their children, production traveled to Leach Pond at Borderland State Park in Massachusetts. To make the horrific discovery feel as tactile and grounded as possible, the team created incredibly lifelike, weighted practical dummies cast directly from the young actors rather than relying on CGI. This allowed Leonardo DiCaprio to physically struggle with pulling the “bodies” from the freezing water, lending a grim, agonizing weight to his performance. DiCaprio has frequently cited the production of Shutter Island as one of the darkest, most emotionally exhausting experiences of his career, specifically because of the profound psychological toll of shooting these deeply traumatic flashback sequences.

Shutter Island (2010), directed by Martin Scorsese, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Mark Ruffalo, Ben Kingsley, Michelle Williams. In 1954, a troubled U.S. Marshal and his new partner travel to a remote psychiatric hospital for the criminally insane to investigate an impossible disappearance, only to uncover dark secrets and question their own sanity.

source_details.synopsis: Shutter Island is a 2010 American neo-noir psychological thriller film directed by Martin Scorsese. The screenplay was adapted by Laeta Kalogridis from the 2003 novel by Dennis Lehane. It follows Deputy U.S. Marshal Edward "Teddy" Daniels and his partner Chuck, who come to the fictional Shutter Island in Boston Harbor to investigate its criminal psychiatric facility after one of its patients goes missing; Daniels has his own ulterior motives for taking the case. The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio and Mark Ruffalo, with Ben Kingsley, Max von Sydow and Michelle Williams in supporting roles.
